tasks.title: Phaistos Disc
tasks.transcript: Listen to a talk from an archaeology professor. Throughout the years, archaeologists have discovered many fascinating artifacts on the Greek island of Crete. One example is the Phaistos Disc, an ancient clay artifact found in the ruins of the palace. It was made in the second millennium BCE. It was discovered in 1908, and it features 241 stamped symbols arranged in a spiral. The symbols include images of animals, tools, and other objects, unlike anything else from the Minoan civilization or any other known writing system. Many experts have tried to interpret the enigmatic symbols. Some suggest they could represent a forgotten language; others think they might represent a calendar or even a religious hymn. Yet no consensus has been reached. Another intriguing thing about the disc is how the makers used stamps to imprint the signs by pressing prefabricated stamps into wet clay. This process is remarkable because it suggests a level of sophistication similar to early printing. Some scholars hypothesize that the disc might be an import from another culture, an object brought to Crete by traders or travelers. That remains another point of contention surrounding this fascinating artifact.
